scope: Verification of the B2 aggregated decay engine (src/rnglab/nuclear/aggregate.py and its parts) against analytic laws and against the frozen Layer A engine, with healthy generators only. Not an RNG-sensitivity experiment, not evidence about branching processes, criticality or detectors, not a test of H1, H2 or H3, and not part of the Stage D pilot. Every nuclide and parameter is synthetic.
seed_recipe: rnglab.seeds.namespace_seed(namespace, run, scheme, 'physics') for single runs; namespace_seed(namespace, run, scheme, 'physics', f'{r:04d}') for replicate r of ENS-B2, ENS-A and ENS-NAIVE

generators.numpy-pcg64: rnglab.nuclear.NumpyPCG64Source(seed): numpy PCG64 raw 64-bit outputs, seeded with SeedSequence(seed)

layouts.B2 part size: Counts above 2**50 = 1125899906842624 are split into parts of at most 2**50 trials, one uniform each (rnglab.nuclear.binomial.PART_MAX; Boost's incomplete beta returns NaN near n = 2**53)

ENS-B2.role: B2 ensemble: means, variances, covariances, two-time covariances

ENS-A.engine: rnglab.nuclear.simulate_decays (Layer A, frozen), horizon 12, observed on the S2 grid
ENS-A.role: Layer A ensemble for the Layer A / B2 comparison

BIG.role: huge populations: one part (1e12) and 1025 parts (2**60 + 12345)

PC-B1.target: NC1-style BT-STATE at t = 2.0 against the reference half-life 1.0

PC-B2.engine: naive one-step aggregation (study script only): at most one decay per nucleus and interval
targets: BT-STATE at t = 12.0 of the single run
CT-HOMO at t = 12.0 between ENS-NAIVE and ENS-A
PC-B2.role: positive control: a plausible aggregation error

XREF.role: software check: vectorised and reference B2 engines on the same stream

CHECKPOINT.role: software check: resume from a JSON checkpoint

SINK.role: software check: keep_outputs=False with a sink gives the same digest

tests.BT-STATE: counts in every state at every grid time t > 0 against Multinomial(N, p(t)), p from the Layer A matrix exponential; S4 per precursor group; chi-square with the pooling rule (min expected 5)
tests.BT-DECAY: decays of each unstable nuclide over the whole grid against Binomial(N, q_j(T)) (S4: per group), exact binomial
tests.BT-BINS: decays of the first nuclide of each scheme (S4: each precursor) in every grid interval plus 'none' against the multinomial law from decay_probabilities; chi-square, pooling rule
tests.BT-CHANNEL: first-channel decays over the grid given the nuclide's decays, for every nuclide with two or more channels, exact binomial
tests.BT-PHOTON: photons over the grid given the channel's decays, for every channel with photon yield strictly between 0 and 1, exact binomial
tests.BT-NEUTRON: S4: neutrons of each group in every interval plus 'none' against the multinomial with probabilities P_n (q(t_k+1) - q(t_k)); chi-square, pooling rule
tests.BT-PATH: S2: for every source nuclide with two or more path categories, the Pearson statistic of each planned interval's path-category counts against Multinomial(start count, q(delta)) from the engine's decimal laws, on cells fixed before generation from expected counts (minimum expected count 10; design.json, path_tests), summed over the planned intervals and referred to chi-square(summed degrees of freedom). Counts of several intervals are not pooled, because later start counts depend on earlier outcomes
tests.ET-MEAN: ENS-B2: count of each eligible state at t = 2 and t = 8 summed over replicates against Binomial(R N0, p_j(t)), exact
tests.ET-VAR: ENS-B2: sample variance of each eligible state at t = 2 and t = 8 against its exact variance, two-sided, with s^2 referred to a scaled chi-square whose degrees of freedom match the exact mean and variance of s^2 (rnglab.nuclear.moments, comparison.scaled_chisquare_variance_check)
tests.ET-VARSUM: ENS-B2: sample variance of N_j(2) + N_k(2) for every pair of states eligible at t = 2 (it carries Cov(N_j, N_k) given the ET-VAR tests), same method as ET-VAR
tests.ET-VARSUM2: ENS-B2: sample variance of N_j(2) + N_k(8) for j = k eligible at both times and for j = Xa-400 with every k eligible at t = 8 (it carries the two-time covariance), same method as ET-VAR
tests.CT-HOMO: ENS-A against ENS-B2: pooled state counts at every grid time t > 0, 2 x C homogeneity chi-square on cells fixed before generation from the expected counts of either engine (minimum 5; design.json, comparison.cells); a cell empty in both rows contributes 0 and keeps its degree of freedom
tests.CT-VAR: ENS-A against ENS-B2: ratio of the two sample variances of each state eligible at t = 2 against F(nu, nu), two-sided, nu = 2 variance^2 / Var(s^2) from the exact moments (comparison.variance_ratio_f_check); the common scale cancels
tests.CT-VARSUM: ENS-A against ENS-B2: ratio of the two sample variances of N_j(2) + N_k(2) for every pair eligible at t = 2 (it carries the covariance given the CT-VAR tests), same method as CT-VAR
tests.CT-DECAY: ENS-A against ENS-B2: pooled decays of each unstable nuclide in every grid interval plus 'none', homogeneity chi-square on fixed cells as for CT-HOMO
tests.CT-PHOTON: ENS-A against ENS-B2: pooled photons and photon-less decays of every channel with yield strictly between 0 and 1, 2 x 2 homogeneity chi-square on fixed cells as for CT-HOMO
tests.BIG-STATE: BIG: counts at every grid time against Multinomial(N, p(t)), chi-square
tests.BIG-DECAY: BIG: decays of each unstable nuclide over the grid, z-test against N q_j(T) (normal approximation; Berry-Esseen distance below 1e-5 at these sizes)
tests.eligibility: a state is eligible at t when 2000 p_j(t) (1 - p_j(t)) >= 20 (design.json)
tests.applicability: a chi-square test with fewer than two cells after pooling is not applicable and is not run. Applicability never depends on the data: pooling of the goodness-of-fit tests uses fixed totals and exact probabilities, and the cells of BT-PATH, BT-PHOTON-T and the homogeneity tests are fixed in design.json from expected counts, so design.json lists exactly the tests that run. A planned test that cannot be computed is recorded with its error and is a failed item of R1
tests.BT-PHOTON-T: photons per interval given the channel's decays per interval, for every channel with photon yield y strictly between 0 and 1: Pearson statistic sum_c (P_c - y D_c)^2 / (y (1 - y) D_c) over cells of consecutive grid intervals fixed before generation (min(y, 1 - y) times the expected decays of a cell at least 10; design.json, photon_interval_tests), referred to chi-square(number of cells); a cell without decays contributes 0 (conservative). It tests the time allocation of photons, which BT-PHOTON (totals) cannot see. Channels left with one cell have no such test
tests.coverage: Tested second moments: the variance of every eligible state at t = 2 and t = 8 (ET-VAR), the covariances of every eligible pair at t = 2 through the variances of their sums (ET-VARSUM), and the two-time covariances of the 15 pairs in design.json (t = 2 with t = 8) through sums (ET-VARSUM2); against Layer A, the variances of eligible states and of eligible pair sums at t = 2 (CT-VAR, CT-VARSUM). Not tested: any other feature of the joint law across times. A deviation that keeps every marginal law and the tested sums (for example moving probability between cells of the two-time law of t = 2 and t = 8 in a pattern that leaves those sums unchanged) passes the battery; BT-PATH constrains each interval's law given its start counts, which covers dependence carried by the counts but not dependence carried by anything else (such as reused uniforms)
tests.sensitivity: Non-rejection is not equivalence. design.json (sensitivity) gives, for each variance test type, its power at variance ratios 1.1, 1.25, 1.5 and 2 and the ratios detected with power 0.5 and 0.9 at the Holm level; for example a 10% variance error is detected with probability below 0.01

families.NC1: every test on NC1 runs, ENS-B2, the comparison ENS-A / ENS-B2 and BIG

deterministic_checks.D1: every B2 run reads exactly intervals * words_per_interval words and its source counts 8 bytes per word; every Layer A run reads nuclei * 3 * depth words
deterministic_checks.D2: every B2 run: populations conserved and nonnegative, population changes equal inflow minus outflow, decays out of a nuclide at most its start count plus inflow, photons between 0 and the channel's decays (equal for yield 1, zero for yield 0), neutrons equal beta-delayed-neutron decays; every Layer A run satisfies rnglab.nuclear.checks.decay_invariants
deterministic_checks.D3: XREF: identical digests, populations, path counts, decays, photons, neutrons and stream digests in both engines
deterministic_checks.D4: REPLAY: identical digest and stream digest
deterministic_checks.D5: CHECKPOINT: a run resumed from the JSON checkpoint after interval 3 reproduces the digest and the remaining outputs
deterministic_checks.D6: SINK: keep_outputs=False with a sink reproduces the digest and the sink records the populations
deterministic_checks.D7: ENS-B2, ENS-A and ENS-NAIVE: 400 distinct seeds and stream digests each; no Layer A decay at time 0
deterministic_checks.D8: no random numbers: for every scheme, start nuclide and distinct interval length, the decimal interval law and the matrix exponential on the path tree agree within 1e-12, the end-state probabilities agree with the Layer A matrix exponential within 1e-12 (the float64 matrix exponential itself errs by up to 1.6e-13 on the stiff, close-rate scheme S5, confirmed against a 150-digit evaluation before the freeze), the probabilities sum to 1 within 1e-30 and every probability lies in its mean-value bracket; every reference is finite (a non-finite decimal, path-tree or Layer A value fails D8)
deterministic_checks.D9: BIG: 1 part for 1e12 and 1025 parts for 2**60 + 12345 (parts of at most 2**50); populations conserved
deterministic_checks.D10: exactly the tests named in design.json (planned_tests) ran in each family: no planned test was skipped or failed to compute, and no other test entered a family; every test that could not be computed is also listed as a failed item

reading_rules.R1: B2 agreement with the analytic laws and with Layer A: PASS iff D1 to D10 hold and Holm at family-wise alpha 0.01 rejects no test in NC1 and none in NC2. Otherwise FAIL, listing each failed item. The nominal family-wise error is 1% per family; it is a bound only if every p-value is valid. The exact binomial tests are valid; the chi-square, scaled chi-square, F and normal tests are approximations, so the actual false-FAIL rate is estimated by the calibration (R0), not bounded
reading_rules.R2: Sensitivity: PC-B1 rejects its target, and PC-B2 rejects both of its targets, each at p < 0.01 / (size of the NC1 family). If not, R1 is reported with the statement that the battery lacked the declared sensitivity. The other tests on the positive controls are reported descriptively, outside any family.
reading_rules.R3: Descriptive, no verdict: run times, digits used by the decimal laws, largest decimal-versus-matrix-exponential difference, parts and times of the BIG runs.
reading_rules.general: The study runs once from a clean committed tree. Every outcome is reported whichever way it falls. No threshold, size or test changes after generation; a code change after the freeze is an amendment written before any affected number is regenerated.
reading_rules.R0: Calibration, run once after the freeze and before run_verification.py, in its own namespace (calibration); run_verification.py refuses to start without a completed record calibration that ran on the same frozen files, module files and numerical libraries. The calibrated event is the one R1 uses: Holm rejects at least one test of the family, or a planned test cannot be computed. Criterion C1: for NC1 and for NC2, the Clopper-Pearson 95% upper bound of the probability of that event under the null, from the independent null batteries, is at most 0.02. R0 is reported with R1 whichever way it falls. If C1 holds, R0 states that the false-FAIL rate is below 0.02 (95% confidence). If C1 fails, R0 states that the calibration did not establish that the false-FAIL rate is below 0.02, and states that the rate exceeds 0.02 only if the Clopper-Pearson 95% lower bound exceeds 0.02. An R1 FAIL caused only by approximate tests is reported together with that statement; an R1 PASS is unaffected, and no verdict is changed

smoke.output: research/v020-nuclear-b2-verify/smoke/ (not in Git, excluded from every result)

calibration.null: every run of NC1 and NC2 (S1-S5 single runs, ENS-B2 and ENS-A with 400 replicates of 2,000 nuclei, both BIG runs) drawn from the exact laws with numpy's Generator: multinomial over the decimal path categories of each interval, binomial photons given decays; no RNGLab sampler is involved. numpy's samplers are numerical: at counts above 2**53 they return integers on a lattice whose spacing is at most 6.5e-7 standard deviations of the BIG state counts (design.json, calibration_null_lattice), which no BIG statistic can resolve
calibration.evaluation: the planned tests of every battery, through the functions run_verification.py uses (battery, path_tests, ensemble_tests, comparison_tests, big_tests); a battery whose test names differ from design.json stops the calibration
calibration.reported: per family: batteries in which Holm rejects at least one test or a planned test cannot be computed, with the Clopper-Pearson 95% interval (batteries are independent, so this interval is valid); per test: rejections at 1e-2, 1e-3 and the Holm level with per-test Clopper-Pearson intervals; per test type: batteries with at least one rejection of the type, with a Clopper-Pearson interval, divided by instances x level (the type's share of the union bound), and the mean rejections per battery with an approximate interval only (tests within a battery are dependent, so pooled binomial intervals are not used)

order: after the freeze commit, from a committed tree: calibration.py (record) once
commit results/calibration.json and results/attempts/ (the verification refuses uncommitted results outside results/attempts/ and needs the completed record calibration)
record_procedure.threads: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, OMP_NUM_THREADS and MKL_NUM_THREADS exported as 1 before Python starts (in a SLURM batch script, before the srun line); calibration.py also sets them to 1 for its workers and records the inherited values
record_procedure.attempts: each record run holds an exclusive flock on results/attempts/<script>.lock while it runs (the kernel releases it however the process ends; no second attempt can run meanwhile) and publishes results/attempts/<script>-<k>.json atomically (synced temporary file and hard link) before any random number is drawn, then records how it ended (completed, failed, terminated; SIGTERM is caught); its files go to results/attempts/<script>-<k>/ (verification manifests; the SHA-256 of every finished calibration chunk); results are published by a hard link and never overwritten. A record run may start from a tree whose only uncommitted files are those of earlier attempts in results/attempts/
record_procedure.recovery: an attempt that did not complete is rerun from the start on the same commit with the same command; a record still marked 'started' when the lock is free belongs to a process that died and is listed as interrupted in the new record; the seeds are fixed, so the rerun replays the draws of the interrupted attempt (a replay, not a new sample); a rerun on another commit is a protocol deviation and needs --deviation with its reason, recorded in the attempt and the results; calibration.py compares its chunk digests with those of earlier attempts on the same commit (replay_check) and reports any mismatch
record_procedure.statistics_before_completion: none: run_verification.py writes its manifests and results only when the study ends, and calibration.py prints battery counts and times only; the procedure is not blinded beyond that, and since a rerun on the same commit replays the same draws, seeing an interrupted attempt's output cannot change a result
